## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `7c110d9fd011951fc66bd92c5277b1ccc48478b8`
Local-runs: none
Scope: `packages/mcp/src/stdio-data-bridge.ts`, `packages/mcp/src/plugin.ts`, `packages/mcp/src/stdio-data-bridge.disabled-package-every-caller.test.ts`, `packages/mcp/src/stdio-data-bridge.merged-object-reads.test.ts` + read, not reviewed: `packages/runtime/src/action-execution.ts` (`callData`, `refuseUnservedRelationTargets`, `resolveWriteResponseSchema`, `packageDisabledPredicate`), `packages/core/src/security/effective-object-permissions.ts` (`registryObjectPackageDisabled`), `packages/core/src/utils/object-package-disabled.ts`, `packages/objectql/src/registry-package-addressing.ts` (`isObjectPackageDisabled`), `packages/objectql/src/engine-summaries-and-expansion.ts` (`expandRelatedRecords`), `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-query-validation.ts` (`servesExpansionTarget`), and the two prose faces as claims: `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx` row 15, `.changeset/36689-mcp-stdio-disabled-package-every-caller.md`
Security-touching: yes

Net diff read against merge base `7ad103a6c0dfb75bea65ffedf1587f8bf09a0c3c`. Card #36689 read whole, ruling 7212906605 included. Every finding below is read from the tree, none measured.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept set of `enforceApiExposure`: right, where it is asked.** The package question now sits above `if (context?.isSystem) return;`, so it is asked of every caller. It covers the addressed object on all six verbs, `aggregateGroups` (through `runAggregate`), the `get_record_context` door (`assertApiExposed`, and its `get` / `query` are the bridge's own), and the record resource in `plugin.ts`. I found no engine call on the bridge or in `plugin.ts` for an ADDRESSED object that is not behind it.
- **One predicate, one refusal: right.** `registryObjectPackageDisabled` and `objectPackageDisabledError` are the ones `callData` uses, and `SchemaRegistry#isObjectPackageDisabled` is the same question the protocol's by-name read asks. The envelope is `callData`'s field for field, and a hop refusal carries `param` as `callData`'s does.
- **Order: right.** Package first, then exposure, at the addressed object and at each hop, as in `callData`.
- **Over-refusal: none found.** A member on a protocol host was already refused with the same code, status and object; only `param` on a hop is new. An enabled package is refused nothing new. An engine without a registry disables nothing, as on the data route. No shipped answer moves beyond the ruled cell.
- **Public surface: none.** `engineObjectPackageDisabled` and the new optional `StdioObjectReads` member live in a module `packages/mcp/src/index.ts` does not export.
- **Accept set of `stdioExpandMap`: wrong, unchanged by this diff.** See M1.
- **Field-map source of the relation walk: differs from `callData`'s.** See S1.

### ② Semver level

`patch` on `@objectstack/mcp` is the right level: `Metadata-protocol: none` takes `patch`, and a breaking non-protocol change ships `patch` with its BREAKING banner and ADR-0087 marker. Both are present, and both declaration lines match the PR body.

Clause-②: no (narrowing) — holds as declared: the diff removes served answers and adds no published export or schema.

Changeset sentences, each judged against the tree:

- Headline and BREAKING paragraph ("refuses a disabled package's data to every caller ... any caller on a host with no `protocol` service, included"): **not true as written.** `query_records` with `expand` still serves it on that host (M1).
- "of the addressed object on every verb": true.
- "of every nested-relation condition's target, at every hop, with the condition's position as `param`": true wherever the walk finds the site; S1 names the case where it finds none.
- "the predicate `callData` asks", "The `objectstack://` record resource asks the same question", "A system context still skips the exposure question", "Nothing else changes for an enabled package": true.
- `Skills-docs: none`: true; no skill or doc page says otherwise.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev note "the system-principal half has no live producer": confirmed. `resolvePrincipal` in `plugin.ts` builds the context from the API key (ADR-0101), never a system context. That half is hardening; the no-protocol half is the reachable one, which is where M1 sits.
- Dev note on the harness (the protocol's by-name read answers an outage for an enabled object and the bridge falls back to the copy): accepted as described. It is the very fallback S1 is about.
- Dev note "full dogfood owed on the final head": still owed; this head will move for M1.
- Check-runs on this head: none failed. 18 were still in progress when read, among them Build Core, Test Core 1 to 10, the three Type Check jobs, and three Lint jobs (one of which runs the system-context census). Those gate verdicts are not in yet, so this record does not stand on them.
- No `open_questions` entry on the card or PR.
- SQL push-down: no finding. The diff adds no id materialisation and no in-app join.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing makes the spec's own refusal real; it takes no declared capability away. A disabled package is off the data plane by the #35526 ruling, and ruling 7212906605 (letter A, 「是，和 callData 一致」) extends that to this door: every caller, every hop, hosts with and without a `protocol` service. At the addressed object and at relation-condition hops the code does what letter A says. Two doors remain, both on the no-protocol host the PR declares closed.

**M1 (must-fix) — `query_records` `expand` still serves a disabled package's records on a host with no `protocol` service.**
`stdioExpandMap` (`stdio-data-bridge.ts`, unchanged) learns that a target's package is disabled only when `readObjectDeclaration` throws the protocol's refusal. On a host with no protocol by-name read that function returns the metadata copy, which cannot refuse. `canServeApiOperation(copy.enable, 'get')` then passes, the target enters the engine's `expand` map, and `expandRelatedRecords` reads the target through `this.find` with no package check (`packages/objectql/src` asks the question nowhere on the read path). The related rows come back nested under the enabled source rows.
In the PR's own harness shape (`withProtocol: false`, package B disabled) this is `bridge.query('dq_alpha', { expand: ['b_ref'], limit: 5 })`: by the code it answers the `dq_beta` row, `secret_note` included, to the member and to the system context.
`callData` never serves this: its protocol arm withholds the expansion by the registry (`servesExpansionTarget`, `!isObjectOfDisabledPackage(registry, target)`), and its no-protocol fallback refuses `expand` with 501. So the bridge does not match `callData` here, and the changeset headline and row 15 ("Lose: nothing of a disabled package ... on a host with or without a `protocol` service") are false in this cell. The docblock line "A target whose package is disabled serves nothing: withheld" is also false on this host.
Fix: in `stdioExpandMap`, ask `reads.isObjectPackageDisabled?.(target)` and withhold the entry, as the data door does. Pin it on the real engine, both hosts, both callers, with a re-enable control that shows the expansion served.

**S1 (should-fix) — the relation walk finds its sites from a read that can come back empty while the engine still lowers the condition.**
`enforceRelationTargetExposure` takes the filtered object's field map from `readObjectDeclaration`: the protocol's by-name read, else the metadata copy. Any throw, or an absent copy, means no field map, no site and no question. `callData`'s walk reads the engine's registry first (`resolveWriteResponseSchema`), "the schema the engine's relation lowering reads". The bridge's own docblock says the copy is absent for a package's boot-registered object on a kernel with an `environmentId`. On such a host with no protocol service, or on a protocol host whose by-name read is out, a condition into a disabled package's object is not refused and the engine lowers it: the 1 / 0 count the #35526 ruling closed. The new tests cannot see this, because the harness hands the bridge a copy of every object.
I could not confirm read-only that a shipped host has that shape, hence should-fix. Fix: read the walk's field map from the engine's registry first, as `callData` does, or fall back to it; pin a hop with the copy absent.

**N1 (nit) — discovery on a no-protocol host.** `list_objects` and `describe_object` there answer from the metadata service, which cannot leave a disabled package's objects out. This is schema, not data, and outside the ruled cell. A follow-up card, not this PR.

Row 15 of `system-context.mdx`: the "Get" half is true against the tree, and the census row (`enforceApiExposure`, one `isSystem` read) still matches. The "Lose" half becomes true once M1 is fixed.

**Verdict: REWORK.** The contract record is a `FAIL` (record 7215079868, tier verified; brief 7215088332). It carries one must-fix and one should-fix, both on the no-`protocol` host. I adopt both. I read M1 in the tree myself.

### What to change

1. **M1 (must-fix, record 7215079868): `query_records` with `expand` still serves a disabled package's rows on a host with no `protocol` service.**
   - `stdioExpandMap` withholds a target only when `readObjectDeclaration` throws `isObjectPackageDisabledRefusal`. With no by-name read, `readObjectDeclaration` returns `readCopy()` (the metadata copy), which never refuses.
   - So the target enters the engine's `expand` map and its rows are served, to a member and to a system context alike.
   - That is the cell this PR claims to close. The changeset headline, its BREAKING paragraph and row 15's "Lose" half are false there.
   - The fix: ask `reads.isObjectPackageDisabled?.(target)` in `stdioExpandMap` and withhold, as `callData` does through `servesExpansionTarget`.
   - Pin both hosts (protocol and no protocol), both callers (member and system), and a re-enable control.
2. **S1 (should-fix, record): the relation walk can find no sites while the engine still lowers the condition.**
   - `enforceRelationTargetExposure` takes its field map from the protocol read or the metadata copy. Where neither answers, it asks no hop.
   - The bridge's own docblock says the copy is missing for boot-registered package objects on an `environmentId` kernel.
   - `callData` reads the engine registry first. Read the hop's field map from the same place, or refuse when it cannot be read, and pin that shape: the current tests hand the bridge a copy of every object.

Both are code moves, so the same reviewer reads the delta.

### Read and clean at this head

- **Shape** (`l1-face.mjs --pr 37900`): open, draft, base `main`, first line `Fixes #36689`. No closing keyword names another card. Declarations: `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: none`. The `Skills-docs:` line is now in the body, a body-only edit at the same head, so the flag is cleared.
- **Changeset level:** `@objectstack/mcp` at `patch` with the BREAKING banner and the ADR-0087 `not-required` marker. The record judges it right: the module has no public export.

  - The row 15 edit in `system-context.mdx`: the "Get" half is true; the "Lose" half is false in the M1 cell.
- **Record-resource gate** (`plugin.ts`): `gateReads` carries the predicate. The resource registers only under a metadata service, so the `gateReads` undefined arm is unreachable, as its comment says.
- **Still owed before an ACCEPT:**
  - Green CI on the delta head. At this reading 18 runs were still pending.
  - The os-dev-report's full dogfood battery, pinned to that head.

### Nit, not blocking

- N1 (record): on a no-protocol host, `list_objects` / `describe_object` still list a disabled package's objects from the metadata service. That is schema, not data, and outside the ruled cell. Follow-up card material.

That closes the walk's fail-open exactly where the engine does lower the condition, it is the answer `callData` gives, and a system context is still asked only the package question. No enabled, exposed target is refused.
